newsitem.title: USA: Boeing says 1997 sales tracking 1996, so far.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says 1997 sales tracking 1996, so far.

text.p: Boeing Co Chairman Philip Condit said Wednesday that his company's commercial aircraft sales this year were running about even with last year, but that some future sales were dependent on the United States renewing favorable trade treatment for China.
Condit gave no figures for 1997 sales, but noted that some recent sales had been made to China and there was a potential there for additional sales.
Condit told a trade conference here that if Most-Favored-Nation trade treatment for China was not renewed, it would have a severe impact on Boeing sales.

Renewed MFN trade treatment for China is to be considered by Congress this summer. Opponents are expected to raise their standard objections based on alleged Chinese violations of human rights and labor rights.
House Speaker Newt Gingrich suggested that renewed MFN be given China for only six months, rather than the 12-month term currently in place.
Condit said that if MFN was not renewed, China would see the United States as an unreliable trading partner and shift some of its purchases to other countries.
This would have an impact on Boeing, he added, because China could move to Airbus Industrie, the European aircraft consortium, to meet its growing aviation needs.
Condit added that lack of MFN would have a wider impact also, with China turning to other suppliers for its other import needs.
